title: Background screening of personnel
status_rationale: No personnel security program, screening records, training records or HR policies were located. Headcount is not established; business plan section 11 is draft.
target_answer: Every person (founder, employee or contractor) who will have access to customer data or production systems completes a background check before access is granted, conducted through an FCRA-compliant consumer reporting agency with applicable state fair-chance procedures: identity verification, criminal history in jurisdictions of residence for seven years, sanctions and exclusion lists, and employment and education verification; enhanced checks (credit history where lawful, fingerprint-based checks where a bank customer requires them) apply to roles with financial-system or privileged access. Checks are repeated every three years and on promotion to privileged roles. Founders are screened like everyone else and results are available to customers in summary under NDA. Access provisioning requires a screening record.
intended_practice: Engage a screening provider; screen the founder and any contractor before production access.
customer_statement: A background screening program is not yet established. We plan to screen all personnel, including founders, before they access customer data.
open_questions: The FCRA and FDIA Section 19 are not seeded as sources.

challenge.customer_intent: People with access to sensitive data are trustworthy.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An insider with a history of fraud misuses data or diverts funds.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Background checks detect only recorded past convictions in searched jurisdictions; most insider incidents involve people without records.
challenge.legally_required: Not for Echelon generally; FDIA Section 19 restricts participation of certain convicted persons in insured depository institution affairs and some banks extend it to vendors.
challenge.contractually_required: Almost universal in financial services vendor contracts.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Operator access to tenant data denied by default (CNV-ARC-002); AI agents and humans cannot execute payments (CNV-LEG-001).
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Provisioning workflow refuses grants without screening record; just-in-time access with approvals.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Access logs and periodic access reviews.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Screening plus structural denial of standing access.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, via access configuration and logs.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unlikely as a replacement; screening remains expected.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Standing privileged access granted for convenience.
challenge.alternative_cost: Medium engineering, already partly in product scope.
challenge.alternative_risks: Break-glass paths still require trusted people.
supporting_arguments: Least privilege limits damage regardless of who the insider is.
opposing_arguments: Customers and examiners treat screening as a baseline hygiene item, independent of architecture.

title: Security, privacy and role-specific training
status_rationale: No personnel security program, screening records, training records or HR policies were located. Headcount is not established; business plan section 11 is draft.
target_answer: All personnel complete security and privacy awareness training at onboarding and annually, covering phishing, social engineering, data handling, incident reporting and acceptable use of AI tools. Engineers complete role training on the Secure Construction Standard rules and the reasons behind them (F# domain types, Strata-only database access, Limen boundary, no HTML input), and personnel handling donor or financial data complete GLBA, privacy and fraud red-flag training. Effectiveness is measured by phishing simulation and by defects caught by gates rather than reviewers. Because the most important rules are enforced by construction, training focuses on judgment that structure cannot provide.
intended_practice: Adopt a training curriculum and tracking before production.
customer_statement: A security awareness and role-based training program is planned but not yet in place.

challenge.customer_intent: Personnel do not cause incidents through ignorance.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Phishing or insecure coding leads to a breach.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Annual awareness training has modest measured effect; secure coding training does not reliably prevent injection flaws.
challenge.legally_required: The FTC Safeguards Rule requires financial institutions to provide security awareness training to their own personnel; customers flow it to vendors by contract.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Restricted interfaces make classes of coding errors unavailable (SEC-DB-001, SEC-UI-001), and phishing-resistant authenticators blunt credential phishing.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Build gates enforce rules regardless of training.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Gate results and phishing simulation metrics.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Structure plus targeted training on residual judgment areas.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely as a complement; completion records are still expected.
challenge.alternative_cost: Engineering cost shared with SEC rules.
challenge.alternative_risks: Overreliance on structure for non-code risks such as social engineering of payment changes.
supporting_arguments: Training time is spent where structure cannot help.

title: Joiner, mover and leaver access lifecycle across all systems
status_rationale: No personnel security program, screening records, training records or HR policies were located. Headcount is not established; business plan section 11 is draft. Unbound requires provisioning and deprovisioning coverage including service and agent identities (SOC2-010).
target_answer: A single identity source drives access to every system: SSO, cloud consoles, code hosting, CI, package registries, AI tool accounts and support tools. Departures trigger revocation of all accounts, sessions, personal access tokens, SSH and API keys within one hour for involuntary and by end of last day for voluntary departures, with secrets the person could see rotated. A daily reconciliation compares active accounts and credentials in every system against the identity source and alerts on orphans. Role changes remove access not needed in the new role. Contractor end dates are recorded at engagement and access expires automatically. Devices are recovered or remotely wiped.
intended_practice: Establish identity source and reconciliation as part of Unbound operations readiness.
customer_statement: An automated access lifecycle with cross-system reconciliation is planned and not yet in place.

title: AI agents as workforce: scope, permissions, accountability and revocation
status_rationale: AI agents perform engineering and research work in Echelon repositories (Praxis provenance records agent actors). Unbound requires agents to be attributable, bounded, monitored and interruptible (SOC2-017), forbids agents from granting themselves permissions or approving their own consequential actions (GOV-AUTH-003), limits agents to propose and prepare (UNB-AGT-002, CNV-AIO-001) and requires prohibited tools to be removed by the tool broker rather than by prompts (UNB-AGT-003). None of this is operating for a production service.
target_answer: AI agents are treated as non-human workforce members with registered identities, a named accountable human owner, a scope statement and least-privilege tool and data permissions enforced by a tool broker, not by prompt instructions. Agents cannot grant themselves access, approve their own changes, merge to protected branches without human or independent-gate approval, or execute consequential actions reserved to humans. Agents have no standing access to production customer data; any access is just-in-time, purpose-bound and logged. Agent credentials and integrations are revoked through the same lifecycle as human leavers. The accountable owner answers for agent outcomes.
current_practice: AI agents do repository engineering and research work. Their permissions, production access and revocation are not documented in records located.
intended_practice: Register agent identities and owners; implement tool broker and approval separation for Unbound operations.
provable: Praxis provenance identifies agent contributions in repositories; nothing proves permission bounds.
customer_statement: Echelon uses AI agents for engineering and research work. A governed model for agent identities, permissions and accountability is planned; agents are intended never to hold standing access to customer production data.

challenge.customer_intent: Work done by AI is controlled at least as well as work done by people.
challenge.adverse_outcome: An AI agent exfiltrates data, introduces malicious or defective code, or takes an unauthorized consequential action.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Personnel controls (background checks, training, NDAs) do not apply to AI agents; questionnaires that ask only about humans miss the risk.
challenge.legally_required: No specific law; AI risk frameworks and some state AI laws address automated decisions, not engineering agents.
challenge.contractually_required: Emerging; increasingly asked in AI addenda.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Tool broker removes prohibited tools; authority matrix refuses agent execution of reserved actions; agents have no production data path by default.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Branch protection and independent gates prevent self-approval.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Provenance and tool-invocation logs per agent run.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Structural permission bounds and provenance rather than human-style vetting.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by inspecting broker configuration, branch protection and logs.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely where customers are educated; uncertain where questionnaires assume human workforce only.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Agents run with a human's broad credentials; prompts relied on for restriction.
challenge.alternative_risks: Prompt injection through data the agent reads; model provider compromise.
supporting_arguments: Agent permissions can be narrower and better logged than human permissions.
opposing_arguments: Customers may be uncomfortable with extensive agent involvement regardless of controls.
A single human accountable owner for many agents may be overstretched.

title: Attribution of AI agent and human work through provenance records
status_rationale: Within repositories governed by Praxis, execution identity records actor kind (agent, human, automation, unknown), stable actor id, provider, model and runtime per execution, and artifact provenance records each contribution keyed by execution (docs/agent-provenance.md in this repository; provenance blocks in this repository's AGENTS.md show agent contributions). Scope is repository work only, not production operations, and the mechanism relies on declared or detected identity and has not been independently reviewed.
target_answer: Every change to code, configuration, policy, agent instructions and evidence is attributed to a stable actor (human, agent with provider, model and runtime, or automation) and to a specific execution, so a customer or auditor can see which work in a release was done by AI agents and which by humans, who approved it, and which instruction and tool configuration the agent ran under. Agent instructions, guardrails and tool permissions are version-controlled and changed only through reviewed changes.
current_practice: Praxis records actor and execution identity for repository work in Praxis-governed repositories. Agent instruction files (such as AGENTS.md) are version-controlled. This is not yet applied to production operations, and agent permission configuration is not centrally recorded.
intended_practice: Extend provenance to release manifests and to Unbound operational agents.
provable: Praxis execution and artifact provenance records in repositories, and Git history of agent instruction files.
customer_statement: In Praxis-governed Echelon repositories, work is attributed to the human, AI agent (with provider, model and runtime where known) or automation that performed it and to the specific execution. This is first-party tooling, applies to repository work rather than a production service, and has not been independently verified.
residual_risks: Identity is declared or detected from environment; a misconfigured runtime records 'unknown' rather than the true actor.
Records live in repositories whose administrators could alter them; tamper evidence is not established.

title: Security leadership, staffing adequacy and segregation of duties in a small team
status_rationale: No personnel security program, screening records, training records or HR policies were located. Headcount is not established; business plan section 11 is draft. No named security officer exists (current-state brief forbids claiming one).
target_answer: A named individual is accountable for information security, with qualifications disclosed, supported by an external security advisor (virtual CISO) under contract until a dedicated hire is justified. Privileged production access is held by at least two named people, with no standing access for routine work. Where one person would otherwise control request, approval and execution, segregation is achieved through independent gates and a second approver (CNV-PLT-010 requires two approvers on control-relevant modules). On-call and incident coverage is contracted with a retained incident response provider for periods when personnel are unavailable. Workload and on-call load are tracked to avoid fatigue in critical operations. Personnel access customer data only from approved jurisdictions.
intended_practice: Engage a security advisor and incident response retainer before production.
customer_statement: Echelon does not yet have a named, dedicated information security officer. Security leadership through an external advisor and an incident response retainer is planned.
residual_risks: With very few people, collusion or a single compromised founder account defeats many segregation controls.
